objective: Enforce the user directive that Citus, OpenSearch, Milvus, ClickHouse, and Iceberg are workload-specific substrate selections rather than universal defaults.
implemented_claims: Added first-class `oya gate validate platform-substrate-defaults` with default path specs/platform-architecture.json.
The gate requires Citus, OpenSearch, Milvus, ClickHouse, and Iceberg rows to be classified as workload-specific-not-universal-default with universal_default=false and selection_required=true.
The gate rejects old universal-default field values for Citus, OpenSearch, and Milvus and requires workload-selected/workload-specific wording.
Platform architecture now records workload-selection policy and workload-specific substrate rows for Citus, OpenSearch, Milvus, ClickHouse, and Iceberg.
Existing vector-store and OLAP advisory lane comments no longer call Milvus/ClickHouse universal canonical defaults.
Masterplan and task projections record the directive for future ChangeSets.
explicit_non_claims: No database, search, vector, OLAP, lakehouse, object-store, or workload runtime is deployed or migrated by this ChangeSet.
No workload selection engine, microservice manifest migration, schema migration, data-plane benchmark, production SLO, or live tenant evidence is claimed.
This does not undo workload-specific existing uses of Citus, OpenSearch, Milvus, ClickHouse, or Iceberg where a service explicitly selects one.
Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required is not claimed green.

red_tests.expected_failure: initial missing-substrate fixture mutation did not remove the Iceberg row; test failed and was corrected before green evidence

verification.command: cargo fmt --all -- --check && cargo check -p oya-dev-cli --all-targets && cargo clippy -p oya-dev-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p oya-governance-gate-catalog-domain && ./bin/oya gate validate planning-closure && JSON parsing
retired-vocabulary/honest-claims scoped corpus plus ./bin/oya git diff --check
broader retired-vocabulary corpus including pre-existing catalog/dispatcher comments

false_green_findings_closed: Platform architecture previously retained universal-looking defaults for Postgres+Citus, OpenSearch, and Milvus; the new gate fails closed on those old exact values.
ClickHouse and Iceberg are now explicitly represented as workload-specific analytics/table-format selections rather than universal OLAP/lakehouse defaults.
Existing advisory lane comments that called Milvus/ClickHouse canonical were corrected to workload-specific language.

A broad retired-vocabulary closeout failed on pre-existing comments in catalog/dispatcher files; scoped retired-vocabulary over changed-new policy text passed and the broad failure was not claimed green.
known_gaps: Repo-wide occurrences may still describe workload-specific service choices such as tenancy/sheets/analytics; this ChangeSet intentionally does not rewrite those service-local decisions unless they claim universal default status.
Future ChangeSets still need API contract SSOT implementation, Kubewarden policy materialization, and Cloud IaC live render/admission/sync/plan/apply evidence.

findings: Small deterministic JSON/text gate enforces the directive without adding runtime abstractions or dependencies.
Prevents accidental fleet-wide substrate lock-in by requiring explicit workload selection for specialized stores and analytics engines.
Negative tests reject the old universal Citus default and missing Iceberg workload-specific row.
CLI defaults to specs/platform-architecture.json and reports row/field counts for quick remediation.
Focused tests, live gate, catalog tests, fmt/check/clippy, JSON/planning, scoped honest/retired/diff checks pass.

F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Spec plus deterministic gate keeps future agents from reverting to universal defaults.
rejected_reasons: Chat/spec-only records are easier to miss and do not fail closed.

findings: No secrets or tenant data touched; directive reduces blast radius from accidental universal data substrate coupling.
No runtime path affected; gate is bounded JSON/text validation.
Workload-specific substrate selection supports residency/compliance by preventing global store assumptions.
Existing service-local choices remain allowed when explicitly selected; the directive only forbids universal default framing.
Run-all catalog includes the gate so future source-of-truth drift is visible.
Oya VCS claim, RED/GREEN logs, task projections, evidence, and audit-chain rows bind the change to the user directive.
Used Oya VCS claim before edits, avoided raw git/gh, and retained non-claims.

review_findings: No critical/high issue found for source-of-truth gate scope; runtime substrate implementation remains future work.
